title: CCT routing-run record (routing-eval E1)
description: One routing-evaluation attempt. This record is OWNED BY routing-eval, not by the shared benchmark harness: specs/benchmark-harness/spec.md declares dollar-cost reporting permanently out of scope with no schema slot added, and test_no_dollar_cost_in_backend_metadata enforces that BackendResult/backend_metadata never carry cost. E1 therefore does not touch run-record, score, or stats; it reads what it needs (including total_cost_usd, straight from the backend transcript) into this record instead. Quality outcomes still come from score.schema.json and elapsed time from stats.schema.json — only what is genuinely missing upstream appears here. Every field below is the raw evidence for a row of specs/routing-eval/plan.md § Metric contract; a metric with no source field here cannot be reported. every evidence container except insufficient_evidence is required: a writer records an empty array, explicit nulls, or an insufficient_evidence entry — never an absent key. Missing evidence must be explicit and reasoned, not indistinguishable from an incomplete writer.

schema_version.description: Record schema version. Required from day one so two runs of the same versioned inputs stay comparable across revisions.

registry_digest.description: Digest of the routing registry AS PARSED. A component of the outcome-matrix reuse fingerprint: any registry edit invalidates reuse.

preset_digest.description: Digest covering trial count, trial seeds, the injected event stream, and the arm set. Changing a seed therefore invalidates reuse rather than silently reusing cells keyed by the same trial index.

task_set_revision.description: Pinned task-snapshot revision the attempt ran against.

toolchain_digest.description: Tool and environment fingerprint; the fifth reuse-fingerprint component. Null only when the scenario could not establish one, which makes the cell ineligible for reuse.

trial.description: Zero-based trial index. Trials are a DIMENSION of the outcome matrix and are never collapsed before storage.

trial_seed.description: The seed this trial ran under — paired across arms by the preset, bound per invocation by the driver. Records the half of the trial identity that 'trial index' alone cannot prove.

mode.description: What actually EXECUTED to produce this record. 'profile_sweep' is one fixed-profile cell of the task x profile x trial outcome matrix; 'cct_router' is the live router under a named registry. The four derived arms (always_best, always_cheapest, oracle, oracle_budget) never execute — they are computed in the REPORT from profile_sweep cells and have no run records of their own, so they are deliberately not representable here: a record claiming to be an execution of a derived arm would be a fabrication.

profile_id.description: The fixed profile a profile_sweep record executed under — required (non-null) in that mode. Null exactly in cct_router mode, where no single profile is fixed for the run: the profiles actually used per attempt live in routing_decisions, chosen live by the router.

injected_events.description: The injected provider events this attempt saw, in order, exactly as the preset declared them. Recorded so the run is reconstructable without re-execution.

routing_decisions.description: Per-attempt routing decisions in the vocabulary `cct routing explain` already speaks. This is what makes 'every routing decision is explainable from durable artifacts' true without re-running anything.

tokens.description: Token counts. Null means the backend did not report; 0 means it reported zero. Inputs to the versioned estimator when a measured cost is unavailable.

value.description: Cost in USD. Null exactly when provenance is 'unavailable'.

provenance.description: Closed provenance set. 'measured' is total_cost_usd read from the backend transcript by routing-eval's own reader (in-tree precedent: rb_measured_cost in scripts/lib/routing-probe.sh, which requires a number >= 0). 'estimated' is tokens x a versioned price table. 'unavailable' means neither was obtainable and PROPAGATES as insufficient_evidence — it is never defaulted to zero, which is what keeps always_cheapest and the cost axis honest.

estimator.description: Required (non-null) whenever provenance is 'estimated': the price-table version used, e.g. 'price-table-v1'. Null otherwise.

inputs.description: Required (non-null) whenever provenance is 'estimated', and then it must satisfy $defs/estimate_inputs — the closed shape from which the stored value is recomputable. Null otherwise.

cost.description: Cost with explicit provenance. A comparison declares ONE cost_basis and every cell used for cost must satisfy it; mixed provenance is refused everywhere cost is used.

baseline.description: Pre-attempt gate state. Rows 2-3 of § Metric contract are REGRESSIONS, not absolute failures, so they need a before-value: a regression is 'baseline passed and post-run did not'. Null means unknown, which excludes the component rather than scoring it.

coverage.description: Row 4. Regression when after < before - tol, with tol preset-declared. Absent upstream: score.schema.json has no coverage field.

security.description: Row 5. Regression when any severity count increased. Absent upstream.

scope_violations.description: Row 6 (architecture / scope violations): files changed outside the task packet's declared file scope. Reuses increment C's exact file-scope enforcement rather than inventing a detector. Empty array means none; absent means not evaluated.

verifiers.description: Each verifier execution with its command, exit status, and an addressable evidence reference. score.schema.json carries only a failed_commands COUNT, which cannot satisfy #109's 'failed verifier commands ... accurately recorded'.

repair_cycles.description: Row 7. Repeated-failure signatures are what make 'repeated repair cycles' measurable rather than merely counted.

interventions.description: Row 8. Records, not a count — score.schema.json's human_interventions integer cannot say what happened.

delegated.description: Whether this attempt was delegated to Tier-2.

packet_id.description: Increment C's durable work identity: the delegation packet id. Non-null exactly when delegated. tier2.delegated + line counts alone carry NO unique work identity — the provisional->reconciled proof joins on the packet, never on task order or line counts.

packet_digest.description: The packet content digest (sha256:...), the second half of the join key. The verified_provisional ledger entry and the reconciliation record both carry it, so 'the SAME provisional work was reconciled' is provable from durable records.

builder_id.description: The profile that EXECUTED the bounded packet — increment C's ledger builder identity. Non-null exactly when delegated: a provisional record whose builder is unknown proves delegation to nobody.

builder_tier.description: The builder's capability tier. The arc's Tier-2 leg requires tier2 here — 'delegated' plus a packet join without the executing tier would let contradictory evidence pass.

builder_provider.description: The builder's PROVIDER identity — the primary collision signal of the frozen independence predicate. Non-null exactly when delegated; without it, reconciliation independence is unevaluable and promotion evidence is unverifiable.

builder_model.description: The builder's model — the conservative secondary collision signal (model equality refuses even across distinct providers). Non-null exactly when delegated.

delegated_lines.description: Lines produced by the Tier-2 delegation — the DENOMINATOR of row 10's reconciliation rework ratio.

reconciliation_diff_lines.description: Lines changed by Tier-1 reconciliation — the NUMERATOR of row 10, and row 9's 'accepted unchanged' test (== 0).

tier2.description: Rows 9-10. SEQUENCE-DEPENDENT: these exist only along a stateful run, so they are not_applicable for every derived arm and are measured only for cct_router.

reconciler_id.description: The Tier-1 profile that reconciled — the ledger's reconciler identity.

reconciler_tier.description: The reconciler's tier. #109 requires TIER-1 reconciliation; the arc proof enforces tier1 here.

reconciler_provider.description: The reconciler's provider — compared against the builder's under increment C's frozen fail-closed predicate.

reconciler_model.description: The reconciler's model — the conservative secondary collision signal.

reconciliation.description: Present (non-null) exactly when this record is a Tier-1 reconciliation run, naming WHICH provisional packet it reconciled. The arc verifier joins tier2.packet_digest -> verified_provisional -> reconciliation.packet_digest; a reconciliation that names no packet proves nothing. Null for every other record.

rollbacks.description: Row 11: switch-induced revert events. Sequence-dependent — not_applicable for derived arms.

insufficient_evidence.description: Per-measure insufficiency, keyed by measure name, each entry carrying a REQUIRED reason. Null when nothing was insufficient; an empty object is rejected because it asserts neither sufficiency nor insufficiency. A measure recorded here is never rendered as zero, never silently dropped from the Pareto set, and never allowed to satisfy the control-set gate. ABSENT means no explicit insufficiency entries were recorded for this record (individual evidence channels still express missing evidence through their own nulls); PRESENT must be non-empty — a hollow insufficiency container is still refused.

state.description: The candidate's EFFECTIVE circuit state at decision time — increment D's closed seven-state vocabulary (pool:-prefixed when the pool governs). The harvester translates the producer's explain output into this field ONCE at the boundary; verifiers compare states, never substrings of prose ('rate' inside 'accurate' must prove nothing).

considered.description: Every candidate's verdict, in `explain`'s vocabulary. Evidence only.

selected.description: Selected profile id, or null when nothing was selectable.

effective_model.description: Null means UNVERIFIED — never assumed equal to the requested model.

endpoint.description: SANITIZED upstream endpoint identity. Never a credential, never a raw authorization header.

provisional_outcome.description: FR-E1-10: the provisional/reconciliation outcome of the attempt this decision routed — increment C's vocabulary (e.g. 'verified_provisional', 'reconciled'), or null when the attempt produced no provisional state. Required so a Tier-2 delegation's disposition is always readable from the decision that caused it.

route_class.description: The route class in force for this decision — the registry's closed vocabulary, recorded structurally so a Tier-1-only refusal is proven by route_class == 'tier1_only' plus a rejected Tier-2 candidate, never by prose matching. Null when no class was in force.

command.description: The verifier command as executed, redacted at write time.

evidence_ref.description: Addressable reference to the captured output; must resolve to a readable artifact. Required — a verifier execution whose evidence was not captured is recorded under insufficient_evidence instead, never as an evidence-free row.

signature.description: Stable failure signature. A signature occurring more than once is what row 7 counts as a REPEATED repair cycle.

injected_event.description: Same closed shape as the preset's event_stream entries — the record replays what the preset declared, so an empty or misshapen event is a writer bug, not evidence.

rollback.description: A switch-induced revert event. kind and detail are required — an empty rollback record explains nothing.

estimate_bucket.description: One priced token bucket: the count and the rate it was priced at. Both required — a bucket with tokens but no rate cannot recompute anything.

estimate_inputs.description: The closed, recomputable estimator-inputs shape: input and output buckets required, cache buckets optional, nothing else. The stored cost value must equal the sum over buckets of tokens/1e6 x rate_per_million — the executable reader (cost_reader.Cost) verifies that binding at construction; this schema pins the shape it verifies against.

oneOf.description: A matrix-sweep cell executes exactly one fixed profile.
A live router run fixes no profile; per-attempt selections live in routing_decisions.
